Subject: Reserved capacity for inference: sizing, start windows, and term options

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the throughput looked promising. We’re trying to finalize procurement guidance for our Q3 launch and need a clear set of term + start-date options from Redwood so we can model spend and procurement windows. Specifically: 

- Can you outline pricing for 12 / 24 / 36 month reserved commits for a Dedicated GPU pool (approx 20 A100-equivalent GPUs at steady-state)?
- We expect a phased ramp: low traffic in month 1–3, 50% capacity month 4–6, full by month 7. Will Redwood allow staged starts (e.g., start 10 GPUs day 1, scale to 20 by month 7) and pro-rate billing?
- What throughput guarantees or latency SLAs do you offer for reserved pools, and what credits apply on SLO misses?
- If we pre-commit to 24 months, what discount bands do you offer at different GPU counts and any overage pricing?

We are on a tight calendar; procurement needs a formal proposal and SOW no later than 2027-04-25. Can you send a draft SOW and proposed commercial terms this week?

Appreciate it —
Anna Kapoor

Subject: Re: Reserved capacity for inference: sizing, start windows, and term options

Anna — thanks for the clear ask and the spreadsheet. Quick answers up front, followed by a short proposal attached.

1) Term pricing bands (high level):
   - 12 months: baseline price (no long-term discount)
   - 24 months: ~15% list discount versus 12m at the 20-GPU profile
   - 36 months: ~22% list discount and optional front-loaded credits for onboarding

2) Staged starts: yes — we support phased ramping and will pro-rate committed units during the ramp window. We call it a staged-onramp policy: you can define checkpoints (month 0, month 3, month 6, month 7 full). If you reach ramp early we adjust billing forward; if you lag we offer a defined buffer window before moving to full commit billing.

3) SLAs & guarantees: for Dedicated pools we offer throughput SLAs tied to committed GPU slices. Typical commercial offer includes a performance SLO (95th pct p99 token latency target by model class) and a credit schedule: 5% billing credit for SLO miss up to two months in a row, escalating for multi-month regressions. Exact targets depend on model family and sequence length; I included a latency guarantee example in the SOW draft.

4) Overage pricing: overage billed at a discounted on-demand rate (usually list * 1.25 / committed GPU-hour), with volume caps and an option to convert overage to additional reserved units mid-term.

I attached a draft SOW (EpochAI_SOW_v3.pdf) with three commercial scenarios: 12m, 24m, and a 24m hybrid (front-loaded credits + staged onramp) that I think maps to your ramp. If you’re okay I’ll loop in Marissa (sales lead on reserved) to align on final discount bands and credit structure.

Attached: EpochAI_SOW_v3.pdf (pdf, 220KB)

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Karthik — thanks for the rapid turnaround and the SOW. A few follow-ups from our side after reviewing with finance and infra: 

- Discounting: the 15% for 24 months is on the right track but we need stronger economics given our committed volume profile. Can Redwood offer a 20% effective discount on a 24-month commit if we agree to an overage-conversion clause (i.e., any sustained overage beyond 2 months becomes additional reserved capacity at the same rate)?
- Hybrid term ask: we’re open to a 24 month commercial with an initial 18-month operational review and an auto-extension option to 36 months if certain throughput thresholds are met. That helps our procurement.
- Start window: procurement requires a hard option to delay the start date up to 90 days after signing without penalty (to coordinate hardware invoices). Is that negotiable?
- Credits/SLO: we need the SLO credit schedule spelled out numerically (example: p95 latency < 250ms for our medium-sized seqs; credits: 5% month 1, 10% month 2, escalation thereafter).

We can sign a redlined SOW by 2027-04-25 if we get these commercial points clarified — especially the 24m discount and the delayed-start option.

—Miguel
VP Engineering, EpochAI

Looping you in — Miguel (EpochAI VP Eng) pushed back on the commercial bands. They asked specifically for: 1) 20% effective discount on 24m if we allow overage->reserve conversion after sustained overage, 2) a contract start delay up to 90 days, and 3) explicit numeric SLO credits (p95 < 250ms target).

My read: we can offer a 24m with a 17.5% standard discount and the option to go to 20% if we add a simple earn-in clause (overage conversion after 60 days of sustained overage) and a front-loaded onboarding credit equal to 3% of committed spend applied in months 1–3. We should allow a one-time start delay up to 60 days with a longer 90-day exception subject to exec approval — 90 days across the board feels risky from capacity planning.

I’m asking Marissa to confirm margin impact and Sean to confirm SLA/legal for the 250ms p95 target and the credit ladder. If both green, I’ll send a redline SOW with the hybrid commercial option.

Thanks,
Karthik

Karthik / team — reviewed with finance. We can accept the following commercial package to close before 2027-04-25: 

- Offer: 24-month reserved commit for initial 20 A100-equivalent GPUs
- Effective discount: 18% standard on 24m. If EpochAI accepts an overage->reserve conversion clause (sustained overage 60 days), we’ll increase to 20% effective discount.
- Onboarding credit: 3% of committed first-year spend applied across months 1–3.
- Start window: one free 60-day start delay; a 90-day start delay is permitted as an exec-approved exception (we’ll require an explicit capacity reservation notice at signing).
- SLA: we will commit to p95 inference latency < 250ms for the medium model profile as defined in the SOW. Credit ladder: 5% invoice credit month 1 for miss, 10% month 2, and case-by-case escalation beyond.
- Overage: billed at committed-rate * 1.25; option to convert to reserved at the agreed conversion terms.
